restatement: Add a single-tag statement {{SET name = expression}} to the deterministic, no-eval template language. It binds a local to the value that the same evaluator behind ${{ }} computes. The value is kept as it is (an array stays an array). In render a math result is stored as the number the output prints. The local is visible from the tag to the end of its innermost block, is fresh on each FOR iteration and never writes the caller's data. Bad names and bad shapes are located syntax errors at parse time. Lenient mode binds null for missing data and strict mode raises a located missing-variable. The tag is standalone for whitespace, and analyze, spec() and OpenAPI agree with the new tag. The lexer keyword lookup becomes own-property only, and the one evaluator bounds the size of a text after each filter and for a SET value. Templates that were valid before keep their output and errors, except the named exceptions. No existing test expectation changes except the logged surfaces.test.ts amendment.
brief_mismatch: The card says docs_impact none and no living-document edits or deltas, but SET is a user-visible new tag. docs/living/architecture/language-contract.md still says 'SET, INPUT, CALL, macros and partials are not built yet', and its 'Surfaces that agree' section describes spec().blocks as openers with END_ closers only. The project rule says a change to a durable fact is recorded as a delta, and the card's User documentation section was left as the unfilled template (no user_visible, user_docs or waiver). The lead should either add a modify delta for the language contract (and a README/user_docs entry or waiver) or record why none is needed. This is not a finding against the build.
verification_plan: c1: SET of literals, paths, ?? defaults, filter chains and math binds the value; an array SET can be walked by FOR; SET and ${{ }} call one evaluator function (no second copy of the variable logic), so codes and messages match
c2: in render, SET t = 0.1 + 0.2 binds the number that prints (0.3), and IF t == 0.3 agrees; resolveTemplate keeps 0.30000000000000004; /0 and %0 are errors in render only

c3: frame per block (top level, IF/ELSEIF/ELSE branch, WHEN/DEFAULT, each FOR iteration, FOR ELSE body, LIST_ITEM, SECTION, FENCE, ROW/HEADER); an inner rebinding ends with its block; a read before the tag reads data; the root data is never written
c4: lenient mode binds null for a missing name and a later read is found and prints empty; strict mode raises missing-variable located at the SET tag, never 1:1

c5/c6: name validation (@, live loop name with ELSE body excluded, invalid identifier, path, two words) and shape (no name, no =, ==, empty expression) are syntax errors at parse time in every entry and in validate/analyze; __proto__, constructor and toString work as names; END_SET and lower-case set are unknown tags
c7: SET is in STANDALONE_TAGS, takes trim markers and outputs an empty string; a SECTION holding only a SET is omitted under skip_empty

c8: analyze treats the SET name as a local from the tag to the end of the same blocks as the interpreter; expression reads are kind set, optional with ??; a read before the tag or after the block is an input
c9: lexer lookup is own-property only, KEYWORDS is exported with SET and no END_SET, and spec().blocks has SET with no closes
c10: size check after each filter and on the final SET value, for strings only, located at the variable or SET; ${{ }} without filters keeps the old output check
c11: OpenAPI usedIn items have no enum, and a description names the kinds including set
c12/m1: no existing test file changed other than the logged surfaces.test.ts amendment; frozen tests unchanged; gate green
m2/m3: no new dependency, no eval, no template regex, no file read

m5: probe that ${{ }} math, defaults, filters, missing names, prototype names, cyclic/BigInt values and resolve versus render keep base output; check the changed math return path for number round-tripping

But it is an unapproved change to the contract's tests, and the manifest is wrong about the file.

findings.title: Render math output now round-trips through Number(formatNumber(result)) and back to text, which can change ${{ }} math output when the formatted text is not JavaScript's shortest number form

serves.scenario: At base, visitVariable printed formatNumber(result) as is in render. Now evaluateValue returns Number(formatNumber(result)) and visitVariable prints it through valueToString/valueToText. That gives the same text only when formatNumber already emits the shortest round-trip form. If formatNumber prints an exponent-range or very large result in another form, an existing template prints a different text. The language contract says 'integers of any size ... print unchanged', and a fixed 15-significant-digit form of a tiny result is another case. Such a template was valid before, and m5 forbids any output change except the named ones. The st-compat guards cover only 7, 2.5, 0.3, Infinity and NaN.

findings.rubric: m5 / reviewer brief goal-critical question 1 (does every template the base accepted keep its output: math with and without filters, resolveTemplate and render apart)
findings.reproduction: Render in both base 02e8dc84 and head 79dd65d, with data {a: 1, b: 10000000, c: 1e15, d: 1e7}: '${{a / b}}', '${{c * d}}', '${{c * c * c}}' and '${{0 - 0 * a}}'. Compare render outputs byte for byte. Any difference shows the regression. Pinning these rows in st-compat closes the risk either way.
